blocks.text: Goes here. Pre-purchase offer architecture and scaling mechanics. Layering multiple offer types (e.g., combining pre-built starter kits with quantity breaks), subscription-only gating, scaling free gifts proportionately to unit volume, and cognitive cost reduction via price-per-serving or price-per-bottle displays.
• Wireframing the product page accordions or side-cart UX -> 07-LPG
• Evaluating the statistical significance of the offer test -> 09-CRO
why: Demonstrates how to layer multiple offer mechanics (subscription gating + quantity breaks + tiered gifts) while using per-serving pricing to eliminate sticker shock on high-AOV bundles.
topics: [layered offers, quantity breaks, price anchoring, subscription gating, tiered bonus stacking]

Topics. offer mechanics / layered offers, subscription-only gating, quantity break tiers; price anchoring / per-serving breakdowns, per-bottle display; bonus stacking / unlocking sequential free gifts tied to volume (e.g., 1 gift per bag, 3 gifts for 3 bags).

Look for. The AOV and Conversion Rate benchmark formula for scaling: $\text{AOV} \times \text{Conversion Rate} > 250$ (removing the percentage sign). Exact mapping of free gifts to quantity break tiers to increase perceived value.
Skip. General agency pitches, promotional intros, and claims about $10M revenue without structural offer breakdowns.

Goes here. Product page layout, listicle advertorial structures, heatmap-informed CTA placement, delivery expectation promises, side-cart optimization, gamified cart progress bars, and cart reservation urgency timers.
• The economic structure of the quantity break offer itself -> 03-OFF
• Post-purchase email flows triggering from an abandoned cart -> 14-EML
why: Details the exact friction-removal and AOV-boosting UX elements for side carts (progress bars, 1-click cross-sells) and listicle landing pages (high CTA placement).
topics: [listicle structure, cart optimization, friction removal, social proof placement, UX/UI elements]

Topics. page types and section order / listicle advertorials ("7 reasons why"); above the fold / early CTA placement based on heatmaps and scroll depth; proof placement / featured review carousels followed by bulk reviews; friction removal / specific delivery date expectations, organized product detail accordions; cart optimization / sticky checkout buttons, side-cart 1-click cross-sells, gamified free-shipping/gift progress bars, reservation urgency timers (e.g., "reserving order for X minutes"), in-cart subscription upgrades.

Look for. Specific UX placements, such as moving CTAs higher up on listicles because heatmaps reveal low scroll depth. Gamification steps in the cart (unlocking tiers like free shipping, then a free gift).
Skip. Agency self-promotion, vague statements about "crushing it with ad creatives," and general e-commerce platitudes.
Scope mix. 60% baseline (friction removal, accordions, sticky buttons), 40% growth (listicles, gamified carts, in-cart upsells).
